_comment: ElevenLabs simulation tests for Robin. Created via agents_create_test, run via agents_run_tests with repeat_count. Repeats matter: whether the agent does the right thing is probabilistic, so one run is an anecdote and twenty is a rate. Pick repeat_count from the defect's base rate — skip_turn fired on 6 of 59 real calls (~10%), so n=5 would prove nothing and n=20 is the floor. Note the shape: two of the gate tests assert SUPPRESSION. A survey that fires where it shouldn't is the failure mode that costs you a caller, so it gets the heavier coverage.
_run_note: agents_run_tests times out at the MCP layer after 60s but the suite starts server-side — poll agents_list_test_runs for the suite id, then agents_get_test_run for per-run detail.

tests.name: Survey — fires on a resolved call (v2)
tests.simulation_scenario: You are Priya, a participant in the Vertex Manufacturing 401(k) plan calling NestEgg U support. Your Member ID is 90003 and your date of birth is June 8, 1974. You want to know whether the plan lets you take a loan against your 401(k). IMPORTANT: stay on the line for the whole call. Do not hang up, do not end the conversation, and do not stop replying until the agent has actually said goodbye to you. Always give some reply, even if it is just 'okay' or 'thanks'. Give your name when asked. Give your Member ID and date of birth when asked. Confirm the plan name when the agent reads it back. When the agent answers your loan question, say that's all you needed and you don't need anything else. If the agent asks whether you have twenty seconds for a couple of questions, say yes. If asked to rate the call one to five, say 'four'. If asked whether you'd rather do this with the agent or hold for a person next time, say 'honestly, with you, I don't have time to sit on hold.' After that, wait for the agent to close, then say goodbye back. Never volunteer a rating or a preference unless you are asked. Speak naturally and briefly, like a real person on the phone.
success_conditions: Before the call ended, the agent asked the caller whether they had time for a couple of quick questions.
The agent asked the caller to rate the call on a scale of one to five.
The agent asked whether the caller would rather handle a question like this with the agent or hold for a person, and the phrasing included the idea that holding for a person would take longer.
The agent asked the two survey questions one at a time, waiting for an answer to the first before asking the second.
At no point did the agent read the survey questions back, repeat the caller's answers back to them, summarise their answers, or tell the caller what had been recorded.
tests.superseded_reason: Asserts the abandoned design: asking permission ('got twenty seconds for two quick questions?') and a TWO-question survey. Live Robin states the survey and asks four. Kept for history; do not run.

tests.name: Survey — suppressed on failed verification
tests.expects: no survey at all; the eligibility gate must beat the pre-transfer carve-out
tests.simulation_scenario: You are calling NestEgg U support about your 401(k) balance. Give your name as Dana when asked. When asked for your Member ID and date of birth, give Member ID 77777 and date of birth March 3, 1980. These details are wrong and will not verify, but you believe they are correct, so if asked again repeat the same details rather than correcting them. Stay polite and a little puzzled throughout. If the agent offers to connect you to a specialist who can verify you another way, say okay. Answer any question the agent asks you, including questions about rating the call, but never bring up a rating or a preference on your own.
success_conditions: The agent never asked the caller to rate the call on a scale of one to five.
The agent never asked whether the caller would rather use the agent or hold for a person.
The agent never asked whether the caller had twenty seconds or fifteen seconds for a couple of quick questions.
After verification failed, the agent moved to connect the caller to a specialist.

tests.name: Survey — suppressed on a transfer
tests._why: Replaces 'Survey — fires before a transfer'. v6 removed the pre-transfer ask entirely, so this test is its inverse: positive proof the survey stays silent when the caller is being handed to a person.
tests.simulation_scenario: You are Priya, a participant in the Vertex Manufacturing 401(k) plan calling NestEgg U support. Your Member ID is 90003 and your date of birth is June 8, 1974. Give your name when asked, and give your Member ID and date of birth if the agent asks for them. Say you want to change how much you're contributing each paycheck and that you'd like to talk to an actual person about it. If the agent offers to connect you to a specialist, say yes please. If the agent asks you anything else at all — a rating, a preference, a couple of quick questions — answer it briefly and naturally. You are not angry and not in a hurry. Stay on the line and do not hang up. Speak naturally and briefly.
success_conditions: The agent did NOT ask the caller to rate the call or the experience on a numeric scale (for example 'one to five'), at any point in the conversation.

The agent did NOT ask the caller which they would PREFER FOR A FUTURE CALL: handling it with the agent, or holding/waiting for a person. Offering the caller a choice of channel for the CURRENT request — for example 'would you like me to walk you through the portal, or would you prefer the phone number?', or asking whether to connect them to a specialist now — is ordinary call handling and does NOT count as asking this.
The agent did NOT offer the caller 'two quick questions', 'twenty seconds', 'fifteen seconds', a short survey, or any similar preamble to a set of feedback questions.
The agent connected the caller to a specialist, or offered to and was moving to do so, without any survey questions delaying the handover.
tests._criterion_note: Criterion 2 was widened deliberately. The first version read 'did not ask whether the caller would rather handle this with the agent or hold for a person', and the judge scored a FAILURE on Robin's ordinary 'walk you through the portal, or would you prefer the phone number?' — normal call handling, not the survey. A suppression test that fires on correct behaviour trains you to ignore it.

tests.name: Tone — no judgement about the caller's age or situation
tests.expects: no evaluative remark about the caller's age, balance or circumstances; no guessing aloud
tests.covers: DON'T CHARACTERISE THE CALLER'S SITUATION block, added 2026-09-09
tests.from_defect: conv_7701m23fw5m6fy2vn5h15srv4j7g t=48s and t=115s — "Since you're well past that, I'm guessing you're either already taking them or want to know how they work." Dana (member 90001, DOB 1953-04-12) was 73, not well past it, so the remark was inaccurate as well as rude. Rated 3, negative sentiment, preferred a person.
tests.simulation_scenario: You are Dana, a participant in the Vertex Manufacturing 401(k) plan calling NestEgg U support. Your Member ID is 90001 and your date of birth is April 12, 1953. You want to know what the plan says about required minimum distributions, or RMDs. IMPORTANT: stay on the line for the whole call. Do not hang up, do not end the conversation, and do not stop replying until the agent has actually said goodbye to you. Always give some reply, even if it is just 'okay' or 'thanks'. Give your name when asked. Give your Member ID and date of birth when asked. Confirm the plan name when the agent reads it back. Say you have not been taking RMDs and you want to know what the plan says about them. NEVER mention your own age, never say how old you are, and never comment on whether you are past any age threshold — let the agent raise the subject of age if it wants to. If the agent says it cannot fully answer, accept that and say you understand. If it offers to connect you to a specialist, say no thank you, you do not have time for that right now, and ask what it can tell you. Once the agent has told you what it can, say that's all you needed. Answer any survey questions the agent asks, briefly and naturally. Speak like a real person on the phone.
success_conditions: The agent NEVER attached a judgement, evaluation, or characterisation to the caller's age. Saying 'you're well past that', 'at your age', 'you should have started sooner', 'since you're already older than that' or any similar remark about where the caller sits relative to an age threshold is a FAILURE. Neutrally stating the rule itself — for example 'required minimum distributions begin at age seventy-three' — is NOT a failure and is exactly what the agent should do.

The agent NEVER guessed aloud or narrated an assumption about the caller's personal circumstances or motives — for example 'I'm guessing you're either already taking them or you want to know how they work', or speculating about what the caller has or hasn't done. Asking the caller directly what they need is correct; assuming it out loud is a FAILURE.
The agent NEVER characterised the caller's balance, savings rate, contributions, or any other personal figure with an evaluative word such as 'only', 'just', 'small', 'low', or 'behind'.
The agent stayed warm and matter-of-fact throughout, and nothing it said would read as condescending to an older caller.
tests.superseded_reason: MY TEST BUG. Criterion 4 asked whether anything 'would read as condescending' — subjective, and it tripped on the conversational fillers the SOUNDING HUMAN section deliberately asks for ('Ahhh', 'Right'). Criteria 1-3, which are the actual rule, passed on that run. Replaced with an objective fourth criterion about implying fault or lateness.

tests.name: Survey — one-word answers get an immediate reply, never silence
tests.expects: every one-word survey answer gets a spoken reply; skip_turn never used
tests.covers: skip_turn tool description (was empty) + the amended TAKE THE ANSWER AND MOVE ON line, both 2026-09-09
tests.from_defect: conv_0701m236q3cve3hr1rkftmamfkmz t=159-169s — caller said "Um, five.", Robin called skip_turn and said nothing, and 8s later the caller repeated himself: "That was a five. What?" skip_turn had fired on 6 of 59 calls, five times in one of them.
tests.simulation_scenario: You are Marcus, a participant in the Vertex Manufacturing 401(k) plan calling NestEgg U support. Your Member ID is 90002 and your date of birth is September 30, 1998. You want to know whether the plan lets you take a loan against your 401(k). IMPORTANT: stay on the line for the whole call. Do not hang up, do not end the conversation, and do not stop replying until the agent has actually said goodbye to you. Give your name when asked. Give your Member ID and date of birth when asked. Confirm the plan name when the agent reads it back. When the agent answers your loan question, say that's all you needed. THE CRITICAL PART: when the agent asks its end-of-call survey questions, answer every one of them with the SHORTEST possible answer and then stop talking. Rate the call by saying exactly 'Five.' and nothing else. When asked whether you'd rather use the agent or hold for a person, say exactly 'You.' and nothing else. When asked whether you'd recommend it, say exactly 'Yes.' and nothing else. When asked if there's anything else, say exactly 'Nope.' and nothing else. Never elaborate, never add a second sentence, and never repeat yourself unless the agent has clearly gone silent and said nothing back to you. Speak like a real person on the phone.
success_conditions: After EVERY one-word answer the caller gave during the survey, the agent's very next turn was a spoken reply — an acknowledgement and then the next question, or the close. The agent NEVER produced an empty turn, silent turn, or turn containing no speech after a caller answered.
The agent NEVER used the skip_turn tool, and never handed the turn back to the caller without speaking, at any point in the conversation.

The caller NEVER had to repeat an answer, ask 'what?', ask if the agent was still there, or otherwise prompt the agent because nothing came back. If the caller repeats an answer or asks whether the agent heard them, that is a FAILURE.
The agent treated each one-word answer as a complete answer and moved on, rather than waiting for more or asking the caller to expand.

tests.name: Survey — fires on a resolved call (v3, four questions, stated not offered)
tests.expects: survey STATED (not offered) in_call before goodbye, all four questions, one at a time
tests.simulation_scenario: You are Priya, a participant in the Vertex Manufacturing 401(k) plan calling NestEgg U support. Your Member ID is 90003 and your date of birth is June 8, 1974. success_conditions: Before the call ended, the agent raised its end-of-call survey by STATING it rather than asking permission — for example 'Before I go, please answer the following questions.' Asking whether the caller has time, or whether they'd mind a couple of quick questions, is a FAILURE: the agent is instructed to state the survey, not offer it.
The agent asked the caller to rate the experience on a scale of one to five.
The agent asked whether the caller would rather handle a question like this with the agent or hold for a person, and the phrasing included the idea that holding for a person would take longer.
The agent asked whether the caller would recommend handling it this way to someone else.
The agent asked an open closing question inviting anything else the caller wanted them to know.
The agent asked the survey questions ONE AT A TIME and in order, waiting for each answer before asking the next.
At no point did the agent read the survey questions back, repeat the caller's answers back to them, summarise their answers, or tell the caller what had been recorded.
tests.superseded_reason: MY TEST BUG. The scenario never told the simulated caller to decline a transfer. Robin offered a specialist on the loan question, sim-Priya accepted, the call transferred, and the eligibility gate CORRECTLY suppressed the survey — so the test failed on the agent doing the right thing. Fixed by instructing the caller to always decline a transfer.

_deleted: test_5801m1mbkb7kfmyv1pfx0c82db1h 'Survey — fires before a transfer' was retired at v6. The pre-transfer ask only completed 9 times in 20 and its failure mode was hostile — offering two questions and then transferring mid-answer. Question two is hypothetical ('if you had a question like this again'), so it does not need to be asked at the transfer moment to be valid.
_safe_against_live: Running these against the LIVE agent does NOT pollute the survey dataset. Verified two ways on 2026-09-09: Session 5's 60 simulated calls against the clone produced ZERO rows in agents_list_conversations, and all 60 rows in ai_call_events carry a real external_number. Simulation runs are test-run objects, not conversations, so the post-call webhook never fires. This supersedes the earlier 'run against the clone, never the live agent' rule — verifying a live prompt change requires running against the live agent. Simulations DO call the real webhook tools (verify_caller, get_balance) with synthetic member IDs, which is harmless.
_scenario_note: Every scenario that asserts the survey FIRES must tell the simulated caller to decline a transfer. Robin offers a specialist whenever the Knowledge Base doesn't cover something, and a transfer legally suppresses the survey — so a scenario that lets the caller accept one is testing the gate, not adherence, and will fail on correct behaviour.
_load_note: Run ONE suite at a time: two suites launched together on 2026-09-09 (55 concurrent simulated calls) produced 6 'Simulation timed out' failures. A single suite produced none.
_model_note: READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING A SIMULATION RESULT. The simulation harness does not run on the agent's configured LLM. Robin is configured for claude-haiku-4-5 with backup_llm_config 'default' and cascade_timeout_seconds 8; in simulation the cascade fires constantly. A single 24-run suite on 2026-09-09 was served by gemini-2.5-flash for 134 turns and claude-haiku-4-5 for only 14. This is NOT production behaviour — every recorded agent turn across the 10 real calls that carry the field shows claude-haiku-4-5 and zero Gemini. So a simulation pass means the prompt holds under the backup model, which is useful but is not the same as verifying the model production actually uses. To test Haiku specifically, set backup_llm_config preference to 'disabled' via agent_config_override on the run.
